text: Home Bear Bear: The world’s best friend Tired of the hustle and bustle of the city and the stress from the circus, Bear decided to move to the forest to lead a quiet and reclusive life. Here, everything is perfect: he has his own vegetable garden, a colourful flower bed, beehives and a river nearby for fishing. The only spanner in the works was when a little rascal in a pink sundress appeared in his house. At first, Bear wasn’t exactly happy to have her company, but now he can’t imagine his life without her. Able to do just about anything: cook, sew, paint, write a movie and build spaceships. He even got so carried away that he made a time machine, but didn’t use it often. After all, messing with time can be dangerous. When he has some free time, he likes to read, play checkers and chess, complete sudoku and go fishing. He’s not the world’s best athlete, but still likes to ride his bike, roller skate, ski and has even mastered tennis and golf. He can always find a friend in anyone, from crazy kids to lost aliens. He loves to travel and go on hikes – he visited a volcano, travelled around the world and flew to the moon. He can play several instruments. Likes to eat yummy food. Unconditionally in love with Lady Bear and treats her like a true gentleman should. He can’t exactly boast a mountain of muscle on his beautiful body, so he tries to win her with his personality. But, when confronted with such strong love, he might do silly things. Ready to do just about anything for his beloved: build a tennis court, go into space for a star in the sky, appear as a Spanish macho, and even manage to bake a pie and keep Masha away from it. An exemplary friend, the best mentor, a caring uncle and a foster dad. Calm, patient and understanding. Well, until Masha and Panda get up to their old tricks.

Home Panda Panda: Bear’s nephew from China He is a perfect child in every respect: well-read, diligent, clever, well-behaved and calm. He is super independent and organised. He travels from China by train all by himself, never loses anything, and everything is always in perfect order with him – both his suitcase and in his head. He is a great fan of meditation, martial arts and cooking using traditional recipes. He likes to be taken seriously and seem as grown-up as possible, that is probably why he and Bear get along so well and love going camping together. The only bad quality of Panda is that he is maybe a little arrogant and likes to be praised. As soon as they find themselves in the same room, the battle begins! Who is faster? Who is stronger? Who is better? Who is in charge? Who was the inspiration for Louvre paintings? Who gets which bed? These kids can drive Bear crazy with their fighting and yelling, and it all often ends in some angry growling. At the same time, Masha and Panda can make a great team when they have a common goal in mind. Or a naughty scheme!

Home Dog Dog: Wet nosed cutie Happy, cheerful and playful. A very active friend, usually running from Masha with all his might! He likes to hide with Goat in his kennel; he has mastered the hiding way by now! He’s very flexible and smart, so he can even stretch out across the roof, standing on top like a super-ninja! Easy to train with the proper motivation: a well-vetted coach and a bunch of goodies. Although Dog tries to avoid Masha’s antics as much as possible, he often (hoping for a reward…) rushes to help investigate affairs of a galactic scale with her. Home Hare Hare: Carrot thief There are lots of hares around, but this hare is our hare. He lives inside a tree trunk, right next to his friend Squirrel, so he’s always aware of the latest forest news. Since his humble abode is not far from Bear’s, he often makes visits – but not to see Bear, but to see his carrots! A petty thief that can never be discouraged: not a scarecrow, not shouting, not even Masha can scare away the cute criminal. Only in extreme cases will he run away, but not for long, he’ll soon return for "his" yummy carrots. There’s nothing he loves more than a bucket of collected (well, stolen) carrots and even likes to build towers from them, like a veggie Jenga. The latter, by the way, is preferable: with a stick and puck, Hare is quite happy to play on both ice and grass. Thanks to Masha, he has shown himself to be a talented drummer, definitely in a rock band. He also discovered a different hobby – painting Easter Eggs. He has made some real masterpieces.

Home Squirrel Squirrel: The red-tailed messenger Squirrel is always looking down on everything and everybody. Not because she’s arrogant or cocky, but because she lives high up in the trees. Thanks to the good views from the “upper floors”, she and her red-haired friends are always the first to know when something is taking place. Like when there was an unknown egg in the forest, from which Baby Penguin hatched. While observing from high above, Squirrel strictly guards her borders: if something happens that the red-tail doesn’t like, she’ll launch a barrage of pine cones! She’s so accurate that you can’t hide! When something is happening in the forest, Squirrel is always there. Natural curiosity takes over, so her little red tail can be seen in almost every episode, and she’ll never refuse if you ask for help. She’s got quite a range of talents: she played the harmonica, performed at Masha’s rock concert, refereed a hockey match and is a talented photographer. She also takes good care of herself, as she showed up to Masha’s beauty salon “Enchantress”, or dazzled at the ball in a new, very fancy, dress. She even let Masha paint her winter fur coat! Squirrel can mostly be seen talking to her friend Hedgehog, but also likes to gossip with Bunny too!

Home Goat Goat: Always relaxed Cute, quiet and always calm. She loves to chew on her grass and is never in a rush. She’s not a billy goat, so she doesn’t klippity klop along, but stays in the shade and chews her delicious green grass - trying to stay as far away from Masha as possible! She lives by the principle of “Hakuna Matata”, though she doesn’t know what it means, as she doesn’t watch any cartoons. She cares much more about a cabbage leaf. She’s not a billy goat, so she doesn’t klippity klop along, but stays in the shade and chews her delicious green grass - trying to stay as far away from Masha as possible! She lives by the principle of “Hakuna Matata”, though she doesn’t know what it means, as she doesn’t watch any cartoons. She cares much more about a cabbage leaf. She might live a mundane life compared to some of her forest friends, but she can still play the accordion, wear fancy dress and have fun! She likes a good laugh, especially when they’re not laughing at her, but at Rosie. After all, it’s hard not to laugh at her friend getting dressed as a baby and squeezed into a pram. Masha is also funny, especially when she oversleeps and is late for her lessons. The main rule is to stay at a safe distance, or, better yet, hide in the doghouse! It’s the best hiding spot! Overall, our goat friend isn’t very goatish; she’s kind, warm and very peaceful!

Home Tiger Tiger: Circus performer and magician Handsome, strong, and a trickster. Tiger isn’t the kind to stay home; he likes to travel and go on tours, so he’s almost always on the road. He still finds time for his best friend and travels to stay with Bear and play a game of chess or two. He’s the master of humour, and every time he visits Bear, he puts on a mini-performance. He’s emotional, sensitive and loves his hugs. The first meeting with Masha wasn’t a huge success, as he was a little impulsive, but that soon worked itself out. After all, they both love performances! Masha now looks forward to his visits because a visit from Tiger always means fun and adventure! Though we know him simply as Tiger, he’s known by a lot of different names: Mustachioed-Striped, The Famous Bombay Brahmin Yogi, The Apple, Pears and Pineapples conjurer, The Eater of Sandwich Plates and The Curiosity Tamer. For the sake of a good show, he’s willing to jump through hoops, stand on his head or even get sawn in half! He’s so talented that he can even play a game of pool, replacing the balls with cubes, even going as far as to hold a whole tournament! Always the centre of attention, he will always gather a crowd, as people are drawn to his warm heart and soul. Despite all this, he’s far from vain and will happily exchange a noisy party for a quiet evening with his friend.

Home Dasha Dasha: Masha’s beloved cousin She always comes by train, always on time. At first glance, she looks just like her cousin Masha; you couldn’t tell them apart. Bear got them mixed up after she changed into Masha’s clothes. If you look closely, you can spot the differences. They have different hairstyles, hair colour, different outfits, and Dasha’s bad eyes mean that she wears glasses. Though the girls are a little different on the outside, on the inside they’re complete opposites. Looking at how they act, most people wouldn’t believe that they were related. Despite their different personalities, they are best friends and love and appreciate each other very much. So much so that Masha was ready to move to the city! Dasha is strict, responsible, thorough and independent. She likes everything to be in order and follow the “rules”. Because of these qualities, she’s a real smarty-pants and likes to help teach Masha when possible. She knows almost everything: how to make really yummy food, how to teach, what kind of performance is best, and all about different birds. Yes, yes, Dasha knows a lot, but it’s good that Masha doesn’t take her too seriously, otherwise our cartoon would be very boring!

Home Lady Bear Lady Bear: Bear’s true love A true beauty who lives in the forest near Bear. A fan of leisurely strolls in the woods, often with a basket full of berries and fruits. Easy to spot with her trademark umbrella, protecting the lady from the midday sun. She loves to swim, sunbathe, tennis, and ice-skating during the winter months. Very aware of her own attractiveness, she appreciates Bear’s gentlemanly attempts to court her. For a long time, she didn’t give poor Bear the time of day, as happens when you know somebody from school. Nevertheless, she still enjoys visiting Bear for a nice evening: drinking tea, eating homemade berry pie and having a heartfelt conversation, well, unless Masha comes along. Lady Bar is flattered by Bear’s care and his generosity for compliments. She also loves that Bear will do anything for her, even getting a star out of the sky. She knows what she wants and will fiercely defend herself. She will never hesitate to protect herself, certainly against the sun with the help of her trusty umbrella. Not a fan of fuss, noise and disorder, so she tries to keep her distance from the kids of the forest. Despite this, when in the right mood, she will discuss the latest fashion news with the fashionista herself: Masha. Though she may give the impression of an arrogant diva, she is quite the opposite: sociable and empathetic.

Home Rival Bear Rival Bear: The forest’s machoman He’s a real bodybuilder; he loves lifting and wants all the attention. But attention isn’t enough, he needs admiration! Since his first appearance in the series, Rival Bear has shown just how strong and healthy he is. Playing sports, working out and getting his muscles even bigger are just some of his hobbies. Other than his physique, he has nothing to boast about: no sense of humour, no sharp wit, no self-irony or kindness. He’s too narcissistic and selfish. Winning the heart of Lady Bear is one of his favourite pastimes. Maybe it’s just another achievement for him, or maybe it’s to annoy his old acquaintance, Bear. Did you know that Bear and Rival Bear have known each other since childhood? They went to the same music class, which is where the feud began. Nobody says anything, though, not because they’re scared but because they just don’t want to talk to him.

Home Silly Wolf Silly wolf: Clumsy follower Silly Wolf got this name for a reason: he isn’t the sharpest tool in the shed. He could also be called Clumsy Wolf as if he picks up anything with his paws, it’ll be on the floor within 30 seconds. Doesn’t instil fear like a wolf should, instead he’s more a jester, who people pity and not fear. Nobody knows how he met his comrade Sly Wolf, but now they are inseparable. Though Sly Wolf may seem like the leader, Silly Wolf certainly doesn’t see himself as a follower and feels lucky to have a senior colleague who comes up with such master plans. Even if that means that Silly Wolf has to do the less-than-pretty jobs: sticking his tail into an ice hole for fishing, climbing over a fence to find a hen that turns out to be a rooster, or even strapping into an old diving suit to explore the bottom of the river. Not evil, very gullible, thinks with somebody else’s head and always wants the approval of his older companion. He willingly gets involved with Masha’s adventures – he allowed the young painter to use his body as a canvas, changed his hairstyle with the help of Masha’s beauty salon, caught butterflies with a net, and even agreed to go to a ball dressed as a white sheep. Deep down, he would love to swap places with Rosie and be Masha’s new “baby”: playing with toys, having a bubble bath, and having no worries. Very different from Sly Wolf, who is only interested in food and nothing else. Maybe in a parallel universe, Silly Wolf could even be a positive character, even if a little rough around the edges. But he’s now firmly under the thumb of a bully and spends his days living in an old ambulance and catching flies for his friend’s dinner.

Home Sly Wolf Sly wolf: Generator of stupid plans Sly Wolf is an old-timer of the forest, appearing in the very first episode. A loner who strayed from the pack until he became friends with Silly Wolf. In this friendly tandem, he likes to be the leader. The commander of Silly Wolf, periodically hides his mistakes. A disgrace and a bully who is the architect of many grandiose plans, he is always the “brains” behind the madness, but his plans always end in failure. For example, when they decided to steal a hen from a farm but instead stole a poor rooster. Or when they came up with the brilliant idea to create a taxi service, and, with the help of Masha, built a state-of-the-art luxury taxi. Only with one small problem: neither of them can drive. Although Sly Wolf can’t be called evil or aggressive, sometimes he persuades his friend to attack Rosie or some lost sheep. Well, their dark schemes are never a success! Maybe the failures are because he’s permanently hungry, but a difficult childhood can’t be ruled out.

Home Hedgehog Hedgehog: Nicer on the inside At first glance, it might seem like such a tiny character is not so necessary, but try to imagine the forest without him! Hedgehogs, though small and inconspicuous, are very important animals and our prickly friend even more so! If you’re a fan of the series, you’ll know just how often he and his hedgehog friends take part in forest affairs: they brought mushrooms for Masha's “jam”, they helped save the chief mischief maker from her hiccups, and they helped wallpaper Bear’s house. Though he's small in size, he’s far from timid. He lives a very active life, he’s always busy helping out, either alone or with his fellow hedgehogs. For this reason, he doesn’t intentionally get involved in games and tricks, but one way or another he always seems to be involved. Masha is very fond of him, and is more than happy to fill him to the brim with her porridge! She always likes to decorate his needles with bright colours or make him a little train costume for Halloween! Home Penguin Penguin: Bear’s adopted son Nobody knows where the egg came from or how it got to the forest, but Masha found it and brought it to Bear for “hatching”. As soon as he hatched, baby Penguin immediately took Bear as his papa. Masha is his “older sister”; he listens to her and is always happy to play. A friendly, cheerful and very smart boy with a warm personality. He loves flying about in his aeroplane, he’s a flying bird, after all! When he’s up in the air, he sports his trusty helmet and goggles. The rest of the time he likes to wear his woolly hat that his Papa Bear gave him. Unfortunately, he can’t always stay with Bear and Masha, and has to live in Antarctica so as not to get too hot! Due to his regular trips, he’s now a real flying ace!
